tasks.title: Build a lazy-loaded Monaco file explorer and editable workspace
tasks.description:
Outcome: A lazy-loaded editable Monaco workspace with tabs, explorer and diff.

Current implementation: The planner UI exists; the integrated desktop source workspace is planned. Monaco is selected, not a full VS Code extension host.

Implementation responsibility:
- Implement the reviewed prototype design using small typed React components/router patterns for source explorer, tabs, dirty indicators, saved/draft/history selection and diff.
- Load Monaco/workers/language assets on demand and ship them locally; do not rely on a public CDN or replace the existing lightweight Markdown workflow.
- Read/save only through T484 and use the compatible T485 analysis owner; preserve drafts and explicit conflicts on source/event changes.
- Expose actual language capabilities and desktop focus; retain planner responsiveness and document mobile editing limitations without making mobile a library-selection gate.
- Regenerate both tracked web-ui-dist consumers with UI changes and verify installed asset loading.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Code can be edited and safely saved; source/unsaved/historical versions are visually distinct.
- Agent edits during an unsaved draft do not silently replace either version.
- Monaco integration does not create a second LSP or claim general VS Code extension support.

tasks.title: Connect Monaco navigation to shared analysis and planner rationale
tasks.description:
Outcome: Editor navigation connected to current code, prior tasks and applicable rationale.

Current implementation: Syntax highlighting alone cannot explain why code exists, what used it or which constraints later edits must preserve.

Implementation responsibility:
- Wire definition/reference/diagnostic operations to shared verified provider capabilities and explicit document revisions.
- Show source inspector links to introducing/changing tasks, scoped decisions, conventions, callers/impact and relevant test evidence.
- Handle ambiguous/unavailable/stale resolution and historical snapshots without silently converting them into editable current source.
- Preserve project/workspace/target context and bounded lazy retrieval; no second frontend semantic authority.

Acceptance and evidence:
- The T002/T010/T020 function history and slim/functional constraint are inspectable beside current source.
- Syntax-only and unresolved areas display accurate capability limits.
- Navigation stays revision-safe after refactor, target switch or external edit.

tasks.title: Open source locations in the preferred external editor
tasks.description:
Outcome: Open a resolved source location in the user-selected external editor on the correct machine.

Current implementation: An external opener needs configured editor/host semantics; a browser or remote server path is not automatically the user machine path.

Implementation responsibility:
- Define configurable supported opener adapters and capability discovery; do not hard-code one editor or execute unvalidated command strings.
- Open only registered/resolved source locations with explicit workspace/revision and target-machine mapping.
- Explain missing editor/workspace, unsupported remote mapping and historical source cases without claiming success.
- Test the opener contract with isolated fake launchers; do not launch/change the user actual editor during verification.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Preferred editor receives the correct file/location and machine context.
- Unsafe/arbitrary path or argument injection is refused by the owning opener.
- The user can distinguish unsupported mapping from successful open.
